clue.text: Foolish story no bachelor would pass on?

definitions.meaning: a piece of folk superstition passed down as advice
an unmarried man has no spouses, let alone elderly ones, whose stories he could repeat

explanation.surface: A silly yarn that an unmarried man would refuse to repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a bachelor has no wives, old or young, so has no such tale of theirs to pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a widely believed but baseless traditional notion, a classic foolish story.

clue.text: Bird that can drink in flight?

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does
a wing of a building is a flight's counterpart; here a wing is what gives flight

explanation.surface: A riddle about a bird able to take a sip while flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, a crested plover of farmland, is a bird.

clue.text: Harmless deception in chess player's position

parts.note: White is one of the two players in chess
the lie of something is how it is positioned, as a golf ball's lie

explanation.surface: Bluffing about where one's pieces stand in a chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: A small untruth told to spare feelings is by definition a harmless deception.

clue.text: Very big tub holding sulphur

indicators.note: the tub word holds the sulphur symbol inside it, as a container

parts.note: a vat is a large tub or tank
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: An enormous vessel full of sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: immense, enormous.

clue.text: Amphibian that likes licking tongues?

parts.note: licking tongues are flames, and legend held this tailed amphibian could live in fire

explanation.surface: A creature fond of licking with its tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licking tongues' are tongues of flame: medieval lore said this creature lived unharmed in fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The newt-like amphibian of myth thrived in flames, so it 'likes' fire.

clue.text: More silly, leaving leader behind

indicators.note: the comparative word leaves behind its leading letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: dafter means sillier

explanation.surface: Someone sillier than ever, dropping back behind the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: later, following on.

clue.text: English catalogue holds appeal for one wanting the best

indicators.note: the catalogue word holds the appeal word inside it

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An English catalogue that appeals to discerning, snobbish buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is a crossword convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob who believes only the select few deserve consideration wants the best.

clue.text: Top-quality clergyman in Salisbury once

parts.note: prime means of the best quality
a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A first-rate cleric serving in the cathedral city of Salisbury in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury looks like the cathedral city, but it is the Marquess of Salisbury, who led three British governments in the late 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Salisbury was Britain's head of government, an example of the office.

clue.text: Resolution Nero intimated was flexible

indicators.note: the fodder bends into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nero hinted that his firm decision could be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was flexible' rearranges the letters of NERO INTIMATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: firmness of purpose, resolve.

clue.text: Comes back with material falsehoods

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
lies are falsehoods

explanation.surface: Someone answering with untruths about fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: answers, responds.

clue.text: Loft surrounded by extremely large window

indicators.note: the loft word sits inside the letters from the other word, which surround it
the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an attic is a loft

explanation.surface: A loft space with a very large window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'large', L and E, which go round ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A window with criss-crossed leaded panes is called by this name.

clue.text: Grass I worked into intricate pattern

indicators.note: the letter is worked into the pattern word, placed inside it

parts.note: a maze is an intricate network of paths

explanation.surface: Someone weaving grass into an elaborate design.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a cereal, and cereals belong to the grass family.

clue.text: In a hole, having to pay off gradually

parts.note: a mortise is a hole cut to take a tenon in joinery

explanation.surface: Someone in financial trouble who must clear the debt bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a hole' suggests debt; here it is A plus a carpenter's hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a loan in instalments over time is the accountant's meaning.

clue.text: Machine once of the sort used by author

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
a writer is an author

explanation.surface: An old machine of the kind a novelist used.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard device for printing letters on paper, now largely obsolete, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Getting bigger glass

definitions.meaning: increasing in size or apparent size
a lens for enlarging, completing a familiar phrase

explanation.surface: A lens that makes things look larger.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarging, and the word that precedes 'glass' in the name of a reading lens.

clue.text: Check the main line

definitions.meaning: to halt a flow, as of blood
the principal line of descent of a family, or a plant's main stalk

explanation.surface: Checking a railway's chief route.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow; also the trunk of a family tree or plant.

clue.text: Prevented unwelcome growth in the deficit at first

indicators.note: the growth word goes in among the other letters

parts.note: a wart is an unwanted skin growth

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An unpleasant growth in the budget gap was stopped early.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus D (the first letter of 'deficit') holds WART: TH-WART-E-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foiled, frustrated.

clue.text: Stretch back, needing spells of sleep

indicators.note: the word for stretch is read back to front

parts.note: a span is a stretch of time or distance

explanation.surface: Someone stretching out and leaning back for a doze.
explanation.definitionFit: Short sleeps, dozes.

clue.text: Paul ate off table

indicators.note: the letters go off, out of their order, and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paul ate his meal standing away from the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated stretch of level land is called a tableland.

clue.text: Such ethnic clothes on elder — he's fashionable

indicators.note: the words are fashioned anew, giving a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An older man wearing traditional national garb thinks he's stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges ON ELDER HES; 'Such' points to the clue's elder in his Bavarian dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather shorts with braces, traditional Alpine costume.

clue.text: Whip company into powerful growth

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes into the growth word

parts.note: a surge is a sudden powerful increase

explanation.surface: A business driven into rapid expansion by a lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash used for flogging.

clue.text: Type of shrub of the usual quality

definitions.meaning: a plant trained to grow on a single upright stem

explanation.surface: Describing an ordinary bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bush grown on a single tall trunk; also normal or regular.

clue.text: Be afraid to run in late

indicators.note: the run letter goes in the late word

parts.note: late means dead, as in 'the late king'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fearing having to dash in when late.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fear, be apprehensive.

clue.text: A line frequently taken up

parts.note: oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A line of verse often picked up and quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: overhead, carried up high.

clue.text: One badly behaved pupil excluded

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
out means left out

explanation.surface: A badly behaved pupil is shut out of school.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob, an uncouth person.

clue.text: At any time, set off for peak challenge

parts.note: ever means at any time

indicators.note: the letters go off, out of their order

explanation.surface: Climbers ready to set off for the ultimate summit attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is the climber's supreme test.

clue.text: New sailor, one going in circles round lake

indicators.note: the run of pieces goes inside the circle letters

parts.note: circles look like the letter O, two of them here
a tar is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A novice sailor going round and round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Inferior rooms for working actors

parts.note: under means lower or inferior
studies are rooms for working in

explanation.surface: Poor quarters for working performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand-ins who learn a lead role to cover for its performer are actors.
